speaker: Sheldon
text: Why aren't you covering us? We're getting slaughtered out here! Our whole universe was in a hot dense state, then nearly 14 billion years ago, expansion started. Wait, the earth began to cool, the autotrophs began to drool, Neanderthals developed tools, we built a wall.

speaker: Sheldon
text: We built the pyramids, math, science, history, we unraveled in the mystery, it all started with a big bang.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Did you guys see the new budget memo that went out this morning?

speaker: Leonard
text: War is hell. Yeah, more cutbacks.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Unacceptable. It baffles me why they don't simply let some of you go so that there's money available for my research.

speaker: Leonard
text: You know what baffles me, Sheldon?

speaker: Sheldon
text: Based on your academic record, any number of things, I would imagine. Leslie.

speaker: Leslie
text: Hey, guys. Howard, I got the approval for the rapid prototype for you wanted.

speaker: Leslie
text: You scratch my back, I scratch yours.

speaker: Sheldon
text: Oh, uh, no big deal. They gave Leslie control over some unrestricted grant money.

speaker: Leonard
text: Yeah, okay, but what's with the back scratching and the meow?

speaker: Sheldon
text: I believe the back scratching metaphor generally describes a quid pro quo situation where one party provides goods or services to the second party in compensation for a similar action.

speaker: Sheldon
text: The meow! That sounded to me like an African civet cat.

speaker: Sheldon
text: No. Despite what the name suggests, the civet cat is not a true cat.
